steps: Open the CU Boulder Today article (2026-09-16) and find 'Study on delayed sleep-wake phase disorder'
Confirm eligibility: ages 16-40, with delayed sleep-wake phase disorder/late bedtimes OR healthy with typical bedtimes
Apply via the linked 'Get study details and apply' link or email sleep.study@colorado.edu / call 303-735-1923
Complete health screening, then monitor sleep/mood/eating/blood sugar at home for 1-2 weeks
Live in the sleep laboratory on two separate occasions for 51-66 hours each (~4.87 days total), with blood/saliva sampling and reaction-time/mood testing
catches: Compensation is 'up to $2,009' — amount varies with completed visits/procedures
Enormous time commitment: 6.5-week study including two 51-66 hour stays living in the sleep lab (~4.87 days), six in-person visits, plus 1-2 weeks of home monitoring
Most of the lab time is monitored sleep/living, not active tasks — the pay covers the whole commitment
biggest_catch: Up to $2,009 covers a 6.5-week commitment including ~5 days living in the sleep lab — most of that time is passive monitored time, not active earning.
eligibility: Males and females ages 16-40: diagnosis of delayed sleep-wake phase disorder, late bedtimes after 1 a.m., or healthy with typical bedtimes and no sleep concerns.
